utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: While he is, Mr. President, just leftover exhibit issues from this witness. The last article that I used yesterday, 65 ter 33169, at the moment there's not a translation yet. That's pending. So I'd ask that it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33169 receives Exhibit Number P7590.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, second, we've uploaded a new version of the 34th Assembly Session which includes both portions already admitted as P2508, and Mr. Kijac's remarks that we looked at on Monday. We'd ask that the Court Officer be instructed to replace P2508 with 65 ter 02382C, and that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think replacement falls within the -- this earlier decision to admit and that it's now new content which is then part of what was admitted. Mr. Lukic, as always, if you want to further contextualise, you have 48 hours to make any application. Madam Registrar, you're hereby instructed to replace the present content of P2508 with 65 ter 02382C, and a new version is now in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kijac, before you -- before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have received at the -- you have given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. And may I further ask you a very short question: Were you not instructed by the Victims and Witness Section that greeting the accused when you come into the courtroom is not what you're supposed to do? Didn't you receive any guidance in that respect? I have no translation -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did receive those instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you think that you could ignore them? Because the first thing you did this morning is to greet, Mr. Mladic also greeted back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I greeted Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is in exactly the line of sight with Mr. Mladic. But let's leave it to that. Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was in response to Mr. Lukic's greeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did -- nodded first, so Mr. Kijac responded. So maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps to avoid in future misunderstandings of the kind, because Mr. Mladic apparently considered it to be a greeting to him and he responded to that. And that's what -- exactly what we try to avoid. Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P6889.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as it comes up, good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We have a mismatch between the B/C/S and the English on our screens, or I have a mismatch on my screen. And the B/C/S is correct. There we go. If we could have the end of the document in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document Mr. Lukic showed you on direct examination and I'm directing your attention now to the portion he directed your attention to at the end, which reads: "The aggression on Trnovo and the surrounding Muslim villages started at 0830 h in the morning of 31 May 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In that context, if we could have P4150. This is an order coming from the commander of the Kalinovik Tactical Group on the 4th of June, 1992, just a few days later. It begins: "Following the destruction of enemy forces in Trnovo and the taking of town, the enemy forces and populus fled to Muslim villages to the east and west of the Trnovo-Rogatica lines." You don't dispute that, whoever wrote the document Mr. Lukic showed you, there was an attack on Trnovo on Muslim areas and the Muslim population fled after that attack right around the time described in the document, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to read the document through, Mr. Traldi, but it is a clear document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So do you or do you not dispute that there was an attack on Trnovo end of May/beginning of June 1992 and the Muslim population fled?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but on the basis of the document that you have shown me, I see that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we go to the private session for a moment. And if the witness can leave the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We move into private session. And could the witness follow the usher briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber has decided, due to unforeseen circumstances, that we'd not continue our hearing at this moment. How long we will adjourn is uncertain yet. It may be that we resume later this morning. That is a possibility. And if not, if we would not resume later this morning, the -- we'll resume, as far as we can see now, on the 26th of October, that is next Monday, 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, I, but only if we do not resume later today. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We started a bit earlier than initially announced. That was because the Chamber had not sufficiently considered the rule that -- for a period longer than two hours an accused should not be kept in a holding cell here. That's why we started earlier. But we also understand, Mr. Lukic, you're invited to tell us whether we were well informed, that Mr. Mladic waived his right to be present for the remainder of today's session where we will deal with procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you were properly informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And we have a signed written waiver and it will be in the e-court soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then proceed on that basis. First I'd like to briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I see that at least the public gallery is not empty. And anyone who would expect to hear further testimony of a witness, we -- there will be no further witness testimony today and we'll deal with quite a lot of administrative matters. Just to avoid that people in the public gallery would wait for the witness to re-enter the courtroom. Now I have quite list of matters. But the first one, Mr. Lukic, is about your Defence fourth report on Tomasica experts. Again here is a complaint that you haven't received materials you wished to receive and that's not for the first time that we hear it. At the same time, as far as this Chamber is aware, you've never asked our intervention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if the intervention would be needed. I transmitted that -- Ms. Radovanovic's request this morning to my colleague Traldi, what she needs to see here and -- but the request was in B/C/S, so I don't know even if he was able until now to check it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to avoid that in the very end we find that the expert has not received the materials but that not the available means of pressure were applied and that at the very end we end up with empty hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I -- I'm sorry for interrupting. I know that this was sent to us in July and I think something was communicated but I don't know what. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But please pay proper attention to it, that we don't suffer further delays in that respect. Then, first of all, I'd like to deal with guidance on final trial briefs. You would say perhaps a bit early; we do not think it's early. In the Defence's motion which was dated the 23rd of September of this year, the Defence referred to the filing of its final trial brief. Now, while there are still a number of possible evidentiary phases prior to such filing, the Chamber already indicates to the parties that it expects them to be in a position to file their final trial briefs within a number of weeks after the close of the evidentiary phase of this case. Accordingly, work on the final trial briefs should have already commenced and the parties are urged to direct their attention to this matter. In relation to the content of the final trial briefs, the Chamber stresses that the parties should include very specific references to the evidence which allows the Chamber to identify the evidentiary basis for every argument. One last matter. The Chamber noted that both parties introduced evidence regarding the Dayton Peace Agreement in 1995 and wondered whether the existence of an armed conflict throughout the indictment area and period is in dispute. The Chamber would appreciate if the parties could address this issue through a stipulation either on the record or, at the very latest, in their final trial briefs. I'll now move to delivering an oral decision on the Defence objection of the 7th of July of this year. The objection of the 7th of July was that expert witness Ewa Tabeau's evidence in relation to the bodies exhumed from Jakarina Kosa is beyond the scope of the Prosecution's reopening in its case-in-chief. The Defence objection and the submissions of the parties can be found at transcript pages 36783 through 36785. On the 22nd of August of 2014, the Prosecution requested the reopening of its case in-chief in order to present evidence in relation to the Tomasica mass grave. The Chamber granted the reopening in its decision of the 23rd of October, 2014. During Tabeau's testimony on the 7th of July, 2015, the Defence objected to the Prosecution leading evidence in relation to the mass grave at Jakarina Kosa. The Defence submits that Tabeau's evidence in relation to Jakarina Kosa is beyond the scope of the reopening. The Chamber understands the Defence argument to be that the bodies exhumed from Jakarina Kosa are not related to Tomasica and that the information regarding these bodies was already available to the Prosecution in November 2013, when Tabeau first testified. Therefore, according to the Defence, the Prosecution should not be allowed to adduce this evidence for the first time during the reopening. The Prosecution submits that the bodies exhumed from Jakarina Kosa were already identified in Tabeau's proof of death annex, admitted as Exhibit P2797, and that the link between Jakarina Kosa and Tomasica was set out in paragraph 30 of the Prosecution's motion to reopen, which was granted in full by the Chamber in its 23rd of October decision. The Chamber notes that the bodies exhumed from Jakarina Kosa were included in Exhibit P2797 in connection with the following Scheduled Incidents in the indictment: A.6.1, A.6.4, A.6.6, B.13.1, and B.13.2. Exhibit P2797 was admitted on the 11th of November of 2013. Accordingly, the Chamber finds that there is no merit in the Defence argument that the Prosecution is adducing this evidence for the first time during the reopening. The Chamber further notes that in paragraph 30 of its reopening motion, the Prosecution stated that between 1993 and 1995 some of the remains in the mass grave in Tomasica were removed and taken to a secondary grave in Jakarina Kosa and that DNA confirmed the link between some of the bodies exhumed from the Jakarina Kosa and Tomasica mass grave. Accordingly, the Chamber finds that the link between Jakarina Kosa and Tomasica was contemplated in paragraph 30 of the Prosecution's reopening motion, and because the motion was granted in full, such evidence falls within the scope of the reopening of the Prosecution's case. The Chamber therefore dismisses the Defence's objection. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. I move to my next item which is an oral decision on the admission of P7331. During the testimony of Grujo Boric on 23rd of April of this year, Exhibit Number P7331 was reserved for excerpts [Realtime transcript read in error "experts"] from a previous interview of Boric conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor between the 21st and the 23rd of April, 2004. This can be found at transcript pages 34625 to -626. On the 18th -- 28th of April, the Prosecution submitted that excerpts of that interview should, as a prior inconsistent statement, be admitted for the truth of its content under Rule 89(C) of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. This is be found at transcript pages 34714 to 34720. On the 4th of May, the Defence objected to the admission of the excerpts of the interview without providing reasons for its position. This can be found at transcript pages 35076. I should say "page" because it's only one. On the 28th of August, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence, by e-mail, that it had uploaded excerpts from the interview into e-court under 65 ter number 32422a, and requested this document be assigned to Exhibit Number P7331. On the 21st of September, the Chamber set a deadline of a week for the Defence to make any additional submissions, to which the Defence did not respond. The case law of the Tribunal holds that a witness's previous inconsistent statement may be admitted for the truth of its contents when it fulfils the criteria set out in Rule 89(C) of the Rules of being relevant and of probative value. In determining whether a statement is probative for the purpose of proving the truth of its content, the Chamber may consider the content of the evidence and the circumstances under which it arose. The Chamber hereby refers to its own guidance of the 9th of July, 2012, on transcript pages 527 to 528, and to a decision of the Trial Chamber of the 25th of April, 2005, in the case against Limaj et al., I refer to paragraphs 17 to 21, paragraph 25, and 34, and a decision of the Appeals Chamber of the 1st of February, 2008, in the case of Popovic et al. There it is to be found in paragraph 31. The Chamber having reviews relevant portions of Boric's

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: April, 2015, notes that parts of the interview put to Boric are inconsistent with his testimony. And this can be found on pages 34625 to -628, 34631 to -637, 34641 to -42, and 34683 to 34687. With respect to the first criterion, the Chamber finds that the excerpts of the prior interview selected by the Prosecution are relevant to this case, in particular as they relate to meetings with the Main Staff in 1993, contact between Boric who was the commander of the 2nd Krajina Corps and the accused, and the formation and composition of Crisis Staffs. With respect to the second criterion, the Chamber notes that the interview was not conducted under oath. However, it was conducted by a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor, it was recorded and thus remains available for further review, an interpreter was used, and Boric was informed of his rights and asked if he wished to have a lawyer present. Boric confirmed, under oath during his testimony on the 23rd of April, 2015, excerpts of the interview as truthful and accurate. This can be found at transcript pages 34626 to -627, and 34650. Furthermore, the excerpts of the interview contradicting his testimony were put to him and the Defence had an opportunity to test his knowledge about it during his testimony. Based on the foregoing, the Chamber concludes that the interview has met the requirements of Rule 89(C) of the Rules, and therefore instructs the Registry to attach the document bearing Rule 65 ter number 32422a to P7331 and admits P7331 into evidence for the truth of its content. And this concludes the Chamber's decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At page 16, line 22, the word "experts" appearing in that line should be replaced by the word "excerpts," unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hope everyone will understand having only two eyes that I can't read -- no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not your mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, but I can't read the transcript and my own text at the same time. And there's no suggestion that someone would blame me for it. Then I move to the last decision to be read. And that is the decision on the admission of John Clark's report and annexes, a report and annexes in relation to the exhumation of Tomasica mass grave and the reopening of the Prosecution's case. The documents were marked for identification on the 2nd of July of this year bearing numbers P7443, P7444, P7445, and P7446. On the 26th of August of 2014, the Prosecution filed a notice of disclosure of John Clark's expert report and annexes pursuant to Rule 94 bis(A) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, requesting their admission into evidence. The Defence responded on the 22nd of December, 2014, objecting to the admission of the report and annexes and requesting that John Clark be disqualified as an expert. On the 18th of February, 2015, the Chamber delivered its decision on John Clark's expertise, deferring its decision on the admission of the expert report and annexes until the time of the witness's testimony. This can be found at transcript pages 31932 to -933. Witness Clark testified before the Chamber on the 1st and 2nd of July of this year. Following the conclusion of Clark's testimony, the Defence raised an objection against the admission of the expert report and annexes, submitting that Clark had not been tasked either by the Prosecution or by the Prosecutor's office in Sarajevo at the time he made his observations. As the legal basis for this objection was unclear to the Chamber, it gave the Defence one week to provide additional submissions on this issue. And this can be found at pages 36749 to -752. The Chamber notes that the Defence did not provide the additional submissions it requested. As a result, the objection remains unclear and is dismissed as a result. With respect to the applicable law concerning expert evidence, the Chamber recalls and refers to its 19th of October, 2012, decision concerning expert witness Richard Butler. The Chamber considers John Clark's report to be relevant to, inter alia, the charges relating to the municipalities component of the case and that the conclusions contained in the report fall within the scope of Clark's stated expertise and qualifications. In this respect, the Chamber also observes that during his testimony, the witness recognised the limitations of his expertise and declined to draw certain conclusions; for example, when it concerned the effect a bullet would have on impact after it had travelled specific distances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I made a mistake again, but it's good to be assisted by two colleagues. Yes, the ... I repeat part of my previous sentence. Where I said, for example, when it concerned the effect a bullet would have on impact after it had travelled specific distances. This to be found on transcript pages 36637 to -638. The Chamber considers that John Clark's report may assist the Chamber in understanding issues related to the evidence given on the exhumation of the Tomasica mass grave-site and finds that it has probative value for purposes of its admission into evidence in this case. Accordingly, the Chamber admits John Clark's report and annexes thereto, it's P7443, P7444, P7445, and P7446, into evidence. And this concludes the Chamber's decision. I now move to two remaining issues from the testimony of Bosko Kelecevic. The first one deals with P7462. On 13th of July of this year, P7462 was marked for identification provisionally under seal pending the upload of an excerpt. This can be found at transcript pages 37168 and 37169. On the 25th of August, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence via e-mail that an excerpt has been selected and uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter number 7599a and requested its admission. Mr. Lukic, that was on the 25th of August. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I have in e-court is the full document so I cannot follow that at all. I have 38 pages in both languages. So I don't know what the excerpt is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any response to that, whether the newly uploaded 7599a ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The excerpt is 15 pages in B/C/S and that's uploaded as 7599a. It is not yet assigned P7462 because we haven't gone through the process that we're going through right now yet. So P7462 would still give Mr. Lukic the whole document. But 7599a would give him the selected excerpts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because it has not been -- no instruction has yet been given to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, is it P number or just --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's a 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yeah, 07599a and it is -- it's about 15 pages in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it in the e-court? I'm not getting anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- we have e-court as well. Let's see whether it's there. You said it was 65 ter number 07599a. Mr. Lukic, I find in e-court under this 65 ter number an excerpt from stenographic notes on the 15th Session of the SDC held on the 10th and the 22nd of November, 1993, pages 1 to 8, and 15 to 21. And the original is 15 pages. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we get additional couple of days so -- I really have to go through this. I was not able to locate or maybe a bit confused by the numbers. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Monday is fine if it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Could we do the following. It's just an excerpt of what the complete document, I think, was marked for identification so you can now easily compare. You've had time since the 25th of August. We will admit it but we'll give you an opportunity to revisit the matter by next Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, hereby Madam Registrar is instructed to replace the present document attached to P7462 by the newly uploaded one, 65 ter 07599a, and P7462 is admitted into evidence. I move to the other remaining issue, which is in relation to the testimony of Bosko Kelecevic which is about P7469. On the 13th of July of this year, P7469 was marked for identification pending the provision of a B/C/S translation. This can be found at page 37202. On the 15th of July, the Prosecution advised the Chamber and the Defence via an e-mail that a translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID M000-3014-BCSDT. The Chamber instructs the Registry to attach this translation to P7469 and admits it into evidence. And, as always, Mr. Lukic, you have an opportunity to revisit the matter until next Monday. It's just a matter of translation. I have another question. Earlier the previous document, that was P7462, that was provisionally under seal pending the upload of an excerpt, my question to the Prosecution is whether now, the excerpt being there, whether there's still any need to have it under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Again, it remains -- it would remain tentatively under seal for the same reasons as beforehand, and I'll check if there's any update in that regard. But it's -- the reasons do not change [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Reasons do not change. Therefore, when earlier I admitted P7462 into evidence, the status is that it is admitted under seal. I now to move to a remaining issue from the testimony of Milutin Misic and it's about D1096. On 20th of August of this year, Exhibit D1096 was admitted into evidence. On the 26th of August, the Prosecution e-mailed the Defence requesting that the handwritten title in the heading rows at pages 6 and 7 be translated. On the 23rd of September, the Defence responded advising that the complete translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 1D26-1366. On the 29th of September, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence confirming that it had no objections to the complete translation. The Registry is hereby requested to replace the current translation of Exhibit D1096 with the revised one, of which I just mentioned the number. Next item deals with a remaining issue from the testimony of Ilija Miscevic and it's about the replacement of D1247. On the 22nd of September, 2015, the Chamber admitted into evidence Exhibit D1247, excerpts of Witness Ilija Miscevic's testimony in the Karadzic case. On the 25th of September, the Chamber notified parties that this document contained not only the testimony of Miscevic, but also other excerpts which the Chamber did not intend to admit. In response, the Prosecution uploaded the excerpts of Miscevic's testimony under Rule 65 ter number 32840a. And the Defence, by e-mail, stated that it did not object to D1247 being replaced by this document. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the current version of Exhibit D1247 with document bearing Rule 65 ter number 32840a. I move now to remaining issue from the testimony of Dragisa Masal and I have even a few of them. During the testimony of Dragisa Masal on the 23rd of March, 2015, D958 and D959 were marked for identification pending the provision of B/C/S translations. On the 22nd of September, the Defence advised the Chamber and the Prosecution via e-mail that the translations had been uploaded into e-court under document ID 1D26-1326 and 1D26-1338 respectively. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to attach the corresponding translations to D958 and D959 and admits them into evidence. Also remaining from the testimony of Dragisa Masal is the report from the Los Angeles Times concerning the shelling of Sarajevo which was marked for identification as P7233 on the 19th of March of this year pending a verification of its translation. On the 28th of August, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence stating that CLSS stood by the accuracy of its original translation. On the 16th of September, the Defence was given a deadline of one week to make any additional submissions with regard to the admission of P7233. The Defence has not made any submissions. Therefore, the Chamber admits P7233 into evidence. I move to a remaining issue from the testimony of Bruce Bursik. During the testimony of this witness, documents bearing 65 ter numbers 1D06082, 1D06096, and 25934 were used by the Defence with the witness. Due to the length of the documents, the Chamber asked the parties to agree on excerpts to be tendered in evidence. This can be found on transcript pages 38903 to -907. On the 27th of September, the Defence advised via e-mail that the excerpts were uploaded into e-court under Rule 65 ter numbers 1D06082a, 1D06096a, and 1D06102. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to assign exhibit numbers to these documents. And the Chamber wonders whether there's any objection against admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't think we're able to state a position at this moment and we'll consult, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we do the same that, of course, the matter is pending already quite a while, since late September, that it will be admitted into evidence and that the Prosecution has an opportunity to revisit the matter - it's mainly about excerpts - until Monday. Madam Registrar, could you assign numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D0682a receives Exhibit Number D1322. Document 1D06096a receives Exhibit Number D1323. Document number 1D06102 receives Exhibit Number D1324.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the first time you referred to the document, you read it without a zero. You read 1D0682a which the Chamber understands is a reference to 1D06082a. D1322, D1323, and D1324 are admitted into evidence, and the Prosecution has an opportunity to revisit the matter not later than next week, Monday. I move to a remaining issue from the testimony of Mile Dosenovic, P7508. On the 18th of August of this year, P7508, an information report, was marked for identification because the Defence disputed the determination of an elevation of a building as set out in the report. This can be found at transcript pages 37977 through -979. The Defence did not provide any further submissions despite its assurances that it would come back to the Chamber at the end of that week, being the 18th of September, 2015. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's too late now but we checked it later on. I don't know why it's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have until Monday to -- if you have checked it you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think we do not have any objections anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections anymore. That is then therefore also considered and the Chamber hereby now decides to admit P7508 into evidence. I move to the next item which is a remaining issue from the testimony of Velo Pajic. During the testimony of this witness on the 20th of May of this year, D1061 was marked for identification pending an English translation. I refer to transcript page 35862. On the 28th of September, the Defence advised via an e-mail that it had uploaded the translation into e-court under doc ID 1D26-1430. Any objections as far as the Prosecution is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Again, we'll just ask for a moment to consult, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll proceed as we often do. The Chamber instructs the Registry to attach the translation to D1061 and admits it into evidence. And the Prosecution has an opportunity to revisit the matter not later than next week, Monday. I move on to a remaining issue from the testimony of Simo Tusevljak, and that is the replacement of Exhibit P7525. P7525 was admitted on the 1st of September, 2015, during the testimony of Simo Tusevljak. The B/C/S version of the document contained more pages than the English version, and on the 3rd of September, the Prosecution requested via e-mail that a corrected version uploaded under Rule 65 ter 32976a be assigned to P7525. The Defence e-mailed on the 17th of September stating that it did not object. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to assign P7525 to the correct version of the document. I now move on to remaining issue of the same witness, that is -- relates to the admission of P7527. During the testimony of Tusevljak on 1st of September of this year, P7527, an Official Note of an interview with Dusan Bilcar, was marked for identification pending the provision of a complete translation. On the 3rd of September, the Prosecution informed the Defence and the Chamber via an e-mail that an English translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0105-8653-1-ET. Mr. Lukic, any objections in this respect?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. The Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just reminded that our objection was actually that it's not visible who composed this Official Note. There is no name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have to go back to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- signed but there are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that is something different from a complete translation and that was the reason why it was marked for identification and -- Mr. Lukic, the one who could already raise the matter is the one who can read the B/C/S version because that one was complete. It was an incomplete English translation. So it's a bit unclear, unless you can point at where you already made that objection at the time. I do not fully understand why we should revisit that matter now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will leave it until Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It remains on my pending issues list. Mr. Lukic, you should revisit the matter within one week from now. That means 17 minutes to 1.00 next week, Thursday. Well, if you take until quarter past 2.00, no problem. I now move to a remaining issue from the testimony of John Russell, D1222. During the testimony of John Russell on 7th of September of this year, D1222 was marked for identification pending the upload into e-court of a revised photograph. On the 10th of September, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence indicating that the original photo had been replaced with a revised version on e-court. Mr. Lukic, unless you would have a problem with a new photo, then the Chamber admits D1222 into evidence. The next item is a remaining issue from the testimony of Goran Krcmar. It's documents D1078 through 1080 marked for identification. On the 22nd of May of this year, the Chamber delivered its decision on the admission of associated exhibits tendered through Goran Krcmar. D1078 through D1080 were marked for identification pending CLSS English translations. On the 17th of September, the Defence advised the Chamber via e-mail that, one, translations for D1078 and D1079 had already been uploaded into e-court and attached to the original; and, two, the translation of D1080 had been uploaded under doc ID number 1D26-1322. On the 22nd of September, the Prosecution advised that it had no objections to the translations. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old translation of D1080 with the new one, and admits D1078 through D1080 into evidence. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I could just correct or supplement a matter on which I'd said we were unable to state a position earlier, about ten minutes ago, I think, in today's session. The Chamber referred to documents which had been marked for identification pending an agreement between the parties on excerpts to be selected. Those are the ones that have now been assigned Exhibit Numbers D1322, 1323, and 1324. And I wasn't able to state a position at the time. I'm informed, however, that those are not agreed upon excerpts but are the Defence's proposed excerpts. The discussions remain ongoing and so we'd request that they be marked for identification, not admitted at this time, to allow the discussions that I understood to be contemplated to be completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then check whether the excerpts and the notice that excerpts were uploaded into e-court, whether they mentioned that these were not agreed excerpts but excerpts selected by the Defence only. Now we can do two things. Either we wait for the Prosecution to say what they would like to add or what they would like to be stricken from the excerpts as uploaded by the Defence; and we could wait until finally an agreement will be reached. At the same time, the Chamber is not waiting forever on that. So it gives the parties the choice either to come up with agreement in one week from now -- no, let me give you two weeks. Two weeks from now you can agree on any excerpts. Otherwise, we expect that the Prosecution will make a submission on what they wish to have stricken from the excerpt or what they would like to have added to it. Two weeks from now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we would agree to have anything to be added but we could not have anything stricken. It's from the transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if -- stricken means could be relevance. I mean, the mere fact that the Chamber invited the parties to see what they needed also means that if the parties agree, that the Chamber would usually accept such a selection; but if your selection would still be too broad and not agreed upon by the Prosecution, then the Chamber reserves the right to either send you back and do the same again, or to urge you to seek an agreement with the Prosecution. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We appreciate that, Mr. President, and we'll abide by that schedule and do our best to reach an accord without the need for submissions. Although it -- well, we'll -- we'll cross that bridge when we come to it within the two-week period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the Chamber has no idea why you couldn't reach an agreement and is not interested to know that at this moment. We'd like to look at the results. At the same time, this means that the admission is hereby reversed. Therefore, D1322, D1323, and D1324 now resume the status of marked for identification pending further submissions by the parties and we'll then finally decide on admission, whether or not on exactly the same documentary basis. I move on now to the -- let me see where I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I move on. English translation replacement Exhibit P235. On the 18th of February of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that a revised translation of Exhibit P235 admitted under seal had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0537-6633-A-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the old translation of Exhibit P235 with a new one, and gives the Defence until Monday to revisit that matter. I move to my next item. Replacement of the English translation for Exhibit P3919. Exhibit P3919, a report from the Eastern Bosnia Corps Command, was admitted into evidence pursuant to the Chamber's decision of the 11th of February of 2014. On the 30th of September of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that, one, there was an error on page 2 of the original translation and that the words "bodies" had been mistakenly translated as "corps"; and, two, a corrected translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0113-0142-1-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the previous translation of Exhibit P3919 with the corrected one, and gives the Defence one week from today to revisit the matter. I move to my next item. It concerns translation of Exhibit P2365. On the 22nd of April, 2015, during the testimony of Branko Basara, the Defence indicated that they had concerns with the revised translation of Exhibit P2365, Basara's handwritten history of the 6th Krajina Brigade. To be found at transcript page 34546. The Prosecution understands that the Defence believes the word "capture" should read "liberate." On the 26th of May, the Prosecution e-mailed the Defence and the Chamber requesting that the Defence confirm that this is the only concern it has in relation to the revised translation. The Chamber understands that the Defence has yet to respond. The Chamber gives the Defence one week from today to respond so that the final version of the translation can be requested from CLSS. I move to the next item, which is B/C/S translation replacement P997. On the 20th of February of 2013, Exhibit P997, an UNMO daily situation report, was admitted into evidence. On the 10th of October of 2015, the Prosecution e-mailed the Defence and the Chamber advising that at the time of admission only the two first -- the first two pages of the exhibit were translated into B/C/S and that the complete B/C/S translation was now available under doc ID R008-6174-BCST. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the previous translation of Exhibit P997 with the complete one, and gives the Defence one week from today to revisit the matter. Next item is the English translation replacement of Exhibit P2445. This exhibit, a MUP request dated the 19th of August, 1994, was admitted into evidence on the 3rd of October, 2013. On the 14th of October, 2014, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that, one, the signatory of the original English translation was incorrect as it read Nikola Kesic rather than Nedjeljko Kesic; and, two, a corrected translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID B010-2423-0-ET. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry to replace the previous translation of Exhibit P2445 with the corrected one and gives the Defence one week from today to revisit the matter. I move to a matter remaining of the testimony of Ratko Adzic, P6695. P6695 was marked for identification on the 26th of August, 2014, pending a verification of the English translation and a possible agreement between the parties in this regard. On the 27th of November, the Chamber was informed that CLSS had verified the accuracy of the translation. The Chamber was subsequently informed that no agreement had been reached by the parties. Considering that CLSS has verified the accuracy of the translation, the Chamber admits P6695 into evidence. Another matter remaining from the testimony of Ratko Adzic, P6698, which was also on the 26th of August, 2014, admitted into evidence, and the Chamber invited the Prosecution to make additional submissions with regard to possible discrepancies in the exhibit. The Prosecution filed these submissions on the 10th of March, 2015, informing the Chamber of the proposed corrections and requesting that replacement of the translation by a revised version uploaded under doc ID 0302-0425-1. The Defence did not respond. The Chamber instructs the Registrar to replace the current translation with the revised version and gives the Defence one week from today to revisit the matter. I move to a matter remaining from the testimony of Boro Tadic. On the 17th of December, 2014, P7015 was marked for identification due to its length. On the 11th of September of this year, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence advising that it had uploaded into e-court an excerpt of the document and invited the Defence to suggest the inclusion of additional pages. The Defence did not respond. The Chamber instructs the Registrar to reassign Exhibit P7015 to the newly consolidated document uploaded under 65 ter number 06616a, admits Exhibit P7015 into evidence, and gives the Defence one week from today to revisit the matter, if necessary. I have still three items to go. The first is a matter remaining from the testimony again of Boro Tadic. In the Defence's Rule 92 ter motion for Boro Tadic filed on the 6th of November, 2014, document bearing 65 ter number 1D02034, a book entitled: "To forget about a crime is also a crime," was tendered as an associated exhibit. However, the book was not admitted during the witness's testimony. Could the Defence confirm whether it maintains its request to have the document admitted into evidence? Perhaps you might not be able to immediately respond. We'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will not be able, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One week, Mr. Lukic, you have to respond. And if you finally would insist on tendering, then you are already hereby informed that the Chamber would then invite you to upload an excerpt of the original B/C/S version, which until now is 384 pages, that corresponds with the English translation, which is only 14 pages. We'll hear from you within a week. And if we do not hear from you, Mr. Lukic, we'll consider the document to be withdrawn. Semi-last item. Defence 92 bis motion for Aleksandar Vasiljevic. On the 22nd of September, the Defence filed a Rule 92 bis motion for Aleksandar Vasiljevic, to which the Prosecution responded on the 6th of October. The Defence then filed a request for leave to reply, attaching its reply as an annex, and stating that the Rule 92 bis motion is withdrawn. The Chamber understands that rather than actually replying to the response, the Defence intends to give a notice that it withdraws its motion. This withdrawal is hereby noted by the Chamber. Last one. On the 14th of October of this year, the Defence e-mailed the Chamber and the Prosecution with some suggested revisions to existing translations for the following exhibits: P41, P2930, P4005, P3794, P7260, and P7532. The Chamber invites the Defence to contact CLSS to seek verification and to inform the Chamber if revised translations become available. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to avoid any repetitive work on this, we've forwarded the revisions to CLSS or the requests for revision to CLSS already. There are two documents that we'll communicate with the Defence directly about. One of which I think we've already sent an e-mail about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we can soon expect the final word on these translations. Is there any other matter either party would like to raise at this moment? Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. Last week on the 15th of October, I believe, the Defence filed a motion to reinstate its previously filed 92 ter submission for Witness GRM125. I don't know if the Court recalls the history of that, but there was a filing of the 92 ter, a response by the Prosecution, and then later on a subsequent motion to re-characterise the witness's testimony as 92 bis filed which was rejected. I just wanted to note that in light of those circumstances the Prosecution would, if permitted, simply stand on its previous response to the original 92 ter motion. That response was filed on December 1st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, as you suspected, it was 2014. That's the long history to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now the history comes back to my mind, but, therefore, the Chamber now will rely on the initial response to the 92 ter motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We would use this opportunity only to inform you that although we are beyond our deadline on Ms. Subotic's documents, I just want to inform you that I worked with Mr. Weber on a daily basis to finalize and to -- actually we are trying to cut down as much as possible the documents we will offer into evidence, trying to concentrate them into one police file, instead of having, for example, ten different documents from the same file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any idea when you will --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hope that after -- since I will leading Mr. Poparic the next week, so most probably after he finishes, I will be able to continue to work with that with Mr. Weber. So probably the end of the next week we will continue. Whether we would be able to finish everything, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Shall we put the deadline of the 20th of November for that. That's a long -- a relatively long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I hope that we will finish by that time, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then we expect really to have a response --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- final response. I am aware that you have quite a few deadlines although not all of them that -- creating that much of a burden. Any other matter? If not, we'll adjourn for the day. We will resume Monday, the 26th of October, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 26th day of October, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.07 p.m.,
